definition: The general-purpose processor of a computer, executing instructions sequentially with a few powerful cores — contrasted with the massively parallel GPUs used for ML training.
details: The general-purpose processor of a computer, executing instructions sequentially with a few powerful cores — contrasted with the massively parallel GPUs used for ML training.

explainer.lead: A central processing unit, or CPU, is the main processor that runs a computer's programs by carrying out arithmetic, logic, control, and input/output instructions. It is the general-purpose workhorse of computing, while specialized processors such as GPUs handle different workloads, including massively parallel machine-learning training.

tiers.eli5: A CPU is like a computer's head chef: it reads a recipe one instruction at a time and tells the other parts what to do. It can add numbers, make decisions, and fetch or send information. A computer may have several processor cores, which are like several chefs working in the same kitchen.
tiers.practitioner: CPUs execute general-purpose programs and provide operating-system and virtualization support through dedicated CPU modes. Modern implementations commonly place multiple cores on one integrated-circuit microprocessor, with caches and instruction-level parallelism improving performance; cores may also support multithreading. For ML, do not treat the CPU and GPU as interchangeable: the CPU is suited to general instruction execution, whereas GPUs provide the massive parallelism used for training.
tiers.paperLevel: A CPU is the primary processor whose circuitry executes program instructions, including arithmetic, logic, control, and I/O operations. Its principal components are an arithmetic–logic unit, registers that hold operands and results, and a control unit that coordinates instruction fetch, decode, and execution. Modern designs add caches, instruction-level parallelism, and operating-system and virtualization modes; their general-purpose operation contrasts with the massively parallel GPUs used for ML training.

explainer.example: When a program asks the CPU to add two numbers, the control unit fetches and decodes the addition instruction. Registers provide the two operands to the ALU, which calculates the sum, and the result is stored in a register.

usedIn.name: General-purpose computers
usedIn.detail: Executes the instructions of computer programs and coordinates other components.

usedIn.name: Automobiles
usedIn.detail: Modern microprocessors bring CPU-based computing into vehicles.

usedIn.name: Cellphones
usedIn.detail: Integrated processors run programs within compact electronic devices.

usedIn.name: Embedded systems
usedIn.detail: CPUs appear in microcontrollers and systems on chip, sometimes alongside memory and peripheral interfaces.

explainer.intuition: Think of the CPU as a general-purpose instruction follower with a small set of powerful processing cores. It repeatedly retrieves program instructions, works out what they mean, and coordinates the operations needed to carry them out.
howItWorks: The control unit fetches an instruction from memory.
It decodes the instruction and directs the CPU's components.
Registers supply operands to the arithmetic–logic unit.
The ALU performs the required arithmetic or logic operation.
Registers store results while the CPU coordinates execution and I/O.
explainer.whyItMatters: The CPU is what makes a stored-program computer general-purpose: changing the program in memory changes the task without rewiring the machine. Understanding its sequential, general-purpose role also clarifies why ML training often relies on massively parallel GPUs instead.
misconceptions: A CPU is not the entire computer; memory and I/O circuitry are separate components.
A CPU chip is not necessarily a single core: multi-core processors contain multiple physical CPUs called processor cores.
An integrated circuit containing a CPU can also include memory and peripherals, forming a microcontroller or system on chip.
